10nov.summary: Henri IV tells Béthune that he paid Cardinal Aldobrandini 10,000 écus through Sillery as a gratification after the Parlement's judgment in the Este-Aldobrandini debt, and will pay 10,000 more in the first months of 1602; Béthune is to tell the Cardinal through Cardinal d'Ossat and pretend not to have received the letter.
10nov.en:
Monsieur de Béthune, after the taking of … [the Este–Aldobrandini debt and the Parlement's judgment] … given after
hearing both parties by the Parlement of this city, but I was very glad to have this pretext to gratify the said
Cardinal and show him my goodwill, and that he too should have it for receiving my gratification, so [that] I had ten
thousand écus paid to him at once through the agency of the Sieur de Sillery. As the Cardinal d'Ossat, who knew of
it, will tell you. … Wherefore I have decided to gratify the said Cardinal, to let him know in the prosperity in
which I now find myself by the grace of God that I mean also to acknowledge the kindnesses he has done me just as I
sought his friendship in my necessities.

9nov.summary: A page entirely in cipher about the Spanish news from La Rochepot's secretary and the cardinalate of Don Alexandre, with the cardinals of Joyeuse and d'Ossat. The decryption is decoder output only (about six words in ten); bracketed numbers are open code groups.

22nov.summary: Saint-Germain-en-Laye, answering Béthune's despatch of 29 October: a rebuke of two persons named by code groups for not breaking 'ce coup', the pension of Camaiano to raise the French party in Rome, the Pope's welcome, Barberini's coming, and the baptism of the Dauphin. The clear text is transcribed in full; the 80 cipher runs decode only to fragments.

snip.cap: BnF fr. 3484 f. 34r, the first enciphered passage of Henri IV to Béthune, 10 November 1601
snip.credit: Bibliothèque nationale de France, fr. 3484 f. 34r, via Gallica

system: Villeroy-office cipher: letters as figures and letter-shaped symbols with homophones, marked letters (comma, one or two dots) for words in alphabetical series, two-digit figures for names and syllables.
